Dedup keywords: `filter-ui` operator union · `startsWith` `gt` `lt` · `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES` · plaintext fence · `FilterUISchema`

Surfaced by the `os-dev` seat delivering objectui#7993 (PR objectui#9612). ⚠️ **Filed with its class membership UNPROVEN, on purpose** — see the limits section. ⛔ Not a graded defect yet.

## The reading — verified by the filing seat

`content/docs/components/complex/filter-ui.mdx:40` documents the operator union as:

```ts
    operator?: 'equals' | 'contains' | 'startsWith' | 'gt' | 'lt' | 'between' | 'in';
```

Three of those seven — **`startsWith`, `gt`, `lt`** — are, per the delivering dev's measurement, deprecated **alias** keys in `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES`, whose own doc comment says *"Deprecated: new producers MUST emit the canonical forms; these aliases are a migration bridge and may be dropped in a future major."*

⇒ if that vocabulary is the spec's `ViewFilter` vocabulary, this page teaches three spellings the spec tells authors not to emit — the same class objectui#7993 just repaired one token of.

## ⚠️ TWO LIMITS, stated rather than papered over

**1. Class membership is UNPROVEN.** The delivering dev said plainly that it did **not** verify whether `FilterUISchema`'s operator vocabulary is governed by the spec's `ViewFilter` **at all**. `FilterUI` is a component with its own props; its operator list may legitimately be its own, in which case there is **no defect here**. ⛔ Do not repair this page before answering that question — objectui#7971 is the standing lesson: a literal that *looks like* a spec value is not proof it is one, and acting on the resemblance cost a card.

**2. The filing seat could NOT re-derive the alias membership.** `@objectstack/spec` is not installed in this container's objectui checkout, so the probe is **PREREQUISITE NOT MET**, ⛔ not a negative reading. The alias facts above are the dev's measurement taken inside its own worktree, cited as **theirs**. The page content at `:40` is the filing seat's own reading.

## Why it is worth a card anyway

**Nothing can catch it.** The fence is `plaintext`, so no gate type-checks it — and even a `ts` fence would not have helped: objectui#7993's triage measured that the sibling page's `filter:` block rides a `NamedListView.filter` declared `any[]`, so `check:doc-snippets` judges the deprecated spelling, the canonical spelling and nonsense **identically**.

⇒ this belongs with the standing class — **an authored literal whose enum is never consulted** — alongside objectui#7971, objectui#7713 and objectui#7972.

⭐ **A cheap report-only census is visible and was demonstrated ad hoc**, not built: walk `content/docs` plus package `README.md` files for operator literals and judge each against the spec's exported `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATORS` / `VIEW_FILTER_OPERATOR_ALIASES`. The dev ran exactly that derivation while measuring objectui#7993 — **184 documentation files scanned in under a second, 3 non-canonical literals found**. ⛔ Not built there, and ⛔ not proposed here as scope; recorded for whichever seat rules the objectui#7971 / #7713 / #7972 class, because it is the gate that would have caught all four.
